evidence.quote: Applied to complex Banach spaces regarded as real spaces, the conclusion is real linearity; complex linearity is not asserted.

exclusions.reason: The conclusion asserts real linearity only.

evidence.quote: We use the usual set-theoretic framework with choice here.

exclusions.query: finite executable construction for arbitrary Banach spaces
exclusions.reason: The attainment argument explicitly uses choice and a free ultrafilter; no finite computational representation or runtime is supplied.

hypotheses.statement: Let $X,Y$ be nonzero real Banach spaces and let $f:S_X\to S_Y$ be a surjective isometry. Then $$T(0)=0,\qquad T(x)=\left\lVert x\right\rVert f\left(\frac{x}{\left\lVert x\right\rVert}\right)\quad(x\ne0)$$ is a surjective real-linear isometry. It is the unique linear extension of $f$.

Supports exist, and can be extended with the same norm bound to any specified finite-dimensional enlargement of their domain. If unit vectors $v,w$ and positive numbers $\alpha,\beta$ satisfy $$\left\lVert\alpha v+\beta w\right\rVert=\alpha+\beta,$$ then they have a common support: a norm-bounded linear functional taking value one at both.

If $\left\lVert c\right\rVert<1$, each ray $c+\mathbb R_+v$, $v\in S_X$, meets $S_X$ at a unique point $c+\rho(v)v$. The radius is continuous and satisfies $$1-\left\lVert c\right\rVert\le\rho(v)\le1+\left\lVert c\right\rVert.$$

Let $C$ be a nonempty closed bounded convex subset of a Banach space. If $g:C\to C$ is continuous and, for some $0\le\gamma<1$, $$\chi(g(H))\le\gamma\chi(H)\qquad(H\subset C),$$ then $g$ has a fixed point.

Put $$h=\min\left\{\frac t s,\frac\epsilon u\right\},\qquad
\theta=\frac{hs}{p},\qquad
K=\frac{\left\lVert(r/u)v+hy\right\rVert-\left\lVert(p/s)v+hy\right\rVert}{r/u-p/s}.$$ For every support $\varphi$ at $v+\theta y$, $$\label{eq:K}
\frac\epsilon p\le\varphi(v)\le K\le
\begin{cases}
1-B,& B\le\epsilon,\\
B,& B>\epsilon.
\end{cases}$$
An attained positive maximum as in [eq:maximal] is impossible.

For every bounded nonempty set $H$ in a normed space, $$\chi(\overline H)=\chi(H),\qquad
\chi(\overline{\operatorname{conv}}H)=\chi(H).$$ If $C_n$ are nonempty closed bounded subsets of a Banach space with $C_{n+1}\subset C_n$ and $\chi(C_n)\to0$, then their intersection is nonempty and compact.
Every continuous self-map of a finite-dimensional probability simplex has a fixed point.
Every continuous self-map $g$ of a nonempty compact convex subset $K$ of a normed space has a fixed point.
